investigation_1_adl_parser.question: Does core::language::adl::parse_adl_source (and its helpers lex_adl/collect_block) share the same recursive-descent, unbounded-stack-depth risk RustSemanticExtractor::extract had?
investigation_1_adl_parser.method: read core/src/language/adl/mod.rs directly (1,349 lines) rather than assuming from the module name.
investigation_1_adl_parser.finding: No. lex_adl is a single flat loop over characters/lines producing a token stream; parse_adl_source is a single flat `while index < lines.len()` loop; collect_block tracks brace nesting via a plain integer counter (`depth += clean.matches('{').count() ...; depth -= clean.matches('}').count() ...`), never via a recursive function call. There is no function in this parser that calls itself, directly or indirectly, based on source nesting depth. Arbitrarily deep brace/block nesting in ADL source costs O(depth) TIME (more loop iterations) but O(1) STACK (no additional call frames) -- architecturally immune to this vulnerability class by construction, not merely unobserved to be vulnerable.
investigation_1_adl_parser.action: NO_ACTION -- the open question is closed with a clear negative (no shared risk), not left dangling.

investigation_2_walker_arm_completeness.question: The let-else/`?`/`unsafe` CFG gaps were all found the same way: checking a walker's match arms against the full syn::Expr enum for a variant that silently falls through an unlabeled wildcard. Does the same check, applied to the 7 non-CFG walkers (dataflow/state/effect/concurrency/persistence/ownership/call), find anything similar?
investigation_2_walker_arm_completeness.method: grepped all 38 non-Verbatim syn::Expr variant names (read directly from the vendored syn 3.0.6 source, not from memory) against all 7 walker files, producing a full variant-by-walker occurrence matrix.
investigation_2_walker_arm_completeness.finding: No real gap. Every variant with a 0 count in one or more walkers falls into one of two categories, checked individually, not assumed: (a) the variant is a leaf node with no sub-expression to recurse into at all (Continue -- syn::ExprContinue carries only an optional label, no expr field; Infer -- a bare `_` placeholder; Lit -- a literal value, no substructure) -- there is nothing these walkers COULD recurse into even in principle; (b) the variant is a leaf-like reference (Path) that some dimensions correctly do not special-case because a bare variable/path reference has no bearing on that dimension's own scope (EFFECT/CONCURRENCY/PERSISTENCE do not care whether an expression is 'a bare identifier' the way DATA_FLOW/STATE/OWNERSHIP -- which DO handle Path explicitly, to detect uses/moves -- must). Async/Closure/Const's inconsistent-looking counts (0 in dataflow/concurrency/persistence/ownership, 1 in state/effect/mod.rs) were already investigated and closed in the prior generation: functionally identical (silent skip) across all 7, only 3 document the exclusion with an explicit arm and comment.
investigation_2_walker_arm_completeness.action: NO_ACTION -- no silently-dropped, in-scope, syntax-determined evidence found. This is a genuinely different result from CFG's own three gaps, where the missing arm caused an observably wrong result (an invisible branch); here, every 'missing' arm corresponds to a variant with nothing meaningful to extract for that dimension.
